alt: Email dated July 13, 2026 from L.A. Care Associate Legal Counsel William Seldeen to Nicolas Hernandez, attaching the formal response to the May 28, 2026 Government Claim under reference LMR-8864, and offering to informally resolve the out-of-pocket transportation costs by email.
summary: This document records a formal email thread from L.A. Care's Associate Legal Counsel, Bill Seldeen, dated July 13, 2026. While attaching L.A. Care's formal response to the May 28, 2026 Government Claim, Counsel Seldeen explicitly offers to resolve the out-of-pocket non-medical transportation (NEMT) reimbursement claims informally via email. Forensically, this represents a critical strategic pivot and an admission of exposure, showing that L.A. Care's legal division is seeking to settle out-of-pocket claims through direct negotiations to avoid formal judicial review in Case 26AVSC00542.
full_text:
Gmail

NH <...>@gmail.com

RE: Hernandez - Government Claim [LMR-8864]
1 message

Bill Seldeen <WSeldeen@lacare.org> Mon, Jul 13, 2026 at 9:00 AM
To: "..." <...>@gmail.com
Cc: Felix Huerta <FHuerta@lacare.org>

Dear Mr. Hernandez,

As you know, my name is William Seldeen and I am an attorney for L.A. Care Health Plan.

Please find attached an email copy of L.A. Care's response to your May 28, 2026 government claim. A hard copy will follow by mail. Please give this letter your full attention because it does affect your legal rights.

Unfortunately, based on my review, L.A. Care staff have attempted to reach you by telephone and in writing to obtain information to process your request for reimbursement, but were unable to get the information from you they needed. This is consistent with my experience as well, as you have declined to speak or to send requested records concerning your Conlon claim.

Notwithstanding L.A. Care's response to the government claim, I would be happy to see if we can resolve at least the NEMT reimbursement you are requesting, which we can do by email. To get this started, I would ask for a list of the rides at issue (dates/times, pick up/drop off, out-of-pocket cost, purpose of the ride) for which Call the Car declined your request for transportation.

Alternatively, if you would prefer to work with someone from our staffing team outside the legal department and in writing, please advise.

Sincerely,

William Seldeen
Associate Counsel
L.A. Care Health Plan
